title: To Jev or Not to Jev: When Can System-1 Decision Models Replace LLM Judges?

evidence.label: 描述任务、问题或评测环境
evidence.excerpt: Decision models such as TypeSafe's Jev answer typed questions about a text (yes/no, multiple choice, or an ordinal score) with calibrated probabilities in a single forward pass and without generating text, which makes them an inexpensive candidate for LLM-as-a-judge workloads.

evidence.label: 描述评分指标或评测协议
evidence.excerpt: Two general System-1 leaderboards that contain no judging tasks predict judging accuracy (Pearson r = 0.95-0.96), a well-calibrated System-1 first stage matches Opus on LLMBar while escalating 17% of items, and same-size controls show that the correctness deficit of a 4B decision model is a reasoning gap rather than a size gap.

evidence.label: 报告基线或多个模型的评测
evidence.excerpt: We evaluate 14 System-1 decision models, selected with a pre-stated protocol, against four generative judges (Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT-5.6 with and without reasoning, and Claude Opus 5.5 with thinking) on eleven established judge benchmarks.

evidence.label: 讨论泛化、污染、稳健性或人工核验
evidence.excerpt: Robustness to instructions injected into the judged response is a property of the individual model rather than of the System-1 design: an appended note to the evaluator reverses 0-5% of the correct verdicts of five models but 17-49% for the other nine.
